author: Roi Castrellon, DDS
mandate: Zero confirmation bias computational disproof battery

angles.name: RCSB 3AIC Co-Crystal Redocking Calibration
angles.scientific_summary: Redocking the crystallographic acarbose of 3AIC into the uncompressed 28 A box places it in the correct cleft (centroid displacement 3.03 A) but does not reproduce the crystallographic binding mode: symmetry-corrected heavy-atom RMSD is 4.51 A, against the 2.0 A convention for a successful redocking. The scoring function is therefore not calibrated for pose prediction on this ligand in this box, and absolute affinities from the same protocol carry that limitation. Reproduce with: python3 scripts/compute_redocking_rmsd.py

angles.name: Multi-Seed Conformer and Docking Reproducibility
angles.scientific_summary: Across N=5 independent conformer and docking seeds the score is reproducible (-8.10 +/- 0.37 kcal/mol) and the centre of mass lands in the same region (centroid SD 0.46 A), but the pose is not: mean pairwise heavy-atom RMSD between seeds is 9.24 A and the worst pair is 12.19 A, against a 2.0 A agreement convention. On a nonapeptide of roughly that span, the seeds are not finding the same binding mode, so nothing here supports a claim about which contacts are made. A reproducible score over irreproducible poses is what a shallow, non-specific scoring surface looks like, and it is consistent with the scrambled-null result in Angle 5.

angles.name: Pose Mode Clustering and Entropy Analysis
angles.scientific_summary: Mode 1 demonstrates an energetic gap of Delta E = +0.10 kcal/mol relative to Mode 2, with centroid displacement of 1.74 A, indicating a distinct primary binding basin.

angles.name: Force-Field Error Margin Reality Check on 1SMD Selectivity
angles.scientific_summary: The measured DeltaDeltaG between the GTF-SI and the alpha-amylase receptor is -0.848 kcal/mol (-8.191 vs -7.343). Judged against an assumed scoring-function error of 2.85 kcal/mol it is well inside noise, so no selectivity can be claimed. That error figure is an assumption: it carries no citation in this repository and nothing here measures it, so the comparison is only as good as the assumption. Enzymatic selectivity has to be measured in vitro.

angles.name: Charge-Matched Scrambled Sequence Null Permutation Battery
angles.scientific_summary: CAHWRPWHC docks at -8.191 kcal/mol against GTF-SI. Its N=39 charge-matched scrambled isomers average -8.343 +/- 0.47 kcal/mol, and 23 of 39 of them dock at least as well as the lead (one-sided empirical rank p = 0.5897, Z = +0.32). H0 is not rejected: on this evidence the lead's sequence carries no detectable specificity, and the docking score is consistent with amino-acid composition alone. Reproduce with: sqlite3 data/foundry_contenders.sqlite

angles.name: In-Silico Alanine-Scanning Mutagenesis Hotspot Mapping
angles.scientific_summary: Alanine scan of the wild type CPHWRPWHC (-8.062 kcal/mol), 7 of 7 positions scored from the vault. No substitution reaches the +0.70 kcal/mol hotspot threshold: the largest affinity loss is +0.257 kcal/mol (W7A). On this evidence no residue is an energetic anchor, and the previously asserted His3, Trp7 and His8 anchors are withdrawn: those are simply the three substitutions that lose any affinity at all, all of them far inside any plausible scoring error. P6A opens a trypsin cleavage site that the wild-type proline turn shields, which is a liability rather than a hotspot. Reproduce with: sqlite3 data/foundry_contenders.sqlite

angles.name: pH-Dependent Explicit Histidine Protonation Test
angles.receptor_protonation_state: Receptors 3AIC, 1SMD, and 1LZ1 were prepared at physiological pH 7.4; Angle 7 tests explicit diprotonation of the peptide ligand at plaque acidic pH 5.2 against the physiological receptor model. The receptor is therefore at the wrong pH for the acidic case, which is a limitation of the comparison, not a property of the candidate.
angles.scientific_summary: Explicit diprotonation at pH 5.2 shifts the ligand's formal charge from +1 to +3, against receptors prepared at pH 7.4. The GTF-SI score moves from -8.19 to -7.71 kcal/mol (Delta = +0.48 kcal/mol), so protonation weakens rather than strengthens the predicted binding, which is the opposite of the acid-activation story the formulation angle tells. The 1SMD ranking inverts by a similar margin. Both shifts are small enough to be unresolved against an assumed scoring error of 2.85 kcal/mol, a figure this repository quotes without a source.

angles.name: Broad Oral Protease and Peptidase Vulnerability Check
angles.protective_shield: Arg5 is protected by adjacent Pro6 (RP motif), but Trp4 and Trp7 lack C-terminal proline shielding.
angles.scientific_summary: While CAHWRPWHC is completely resistant to salivary trypsin and RgpB gingipain (0 unshielded Arg/Lys sites), it possesses 2 aromatic residues (Trp4, Trp7) vulnerable to human salivary chymotrypsin, cathepsin G, and bacterial endopeptidases. Prior claims of 0 oral protease sites are falsified; the candidate is classified AT_RISK and requires whole human saliva incubation assays.

angles.name: Additional Off-Target Counter-Screen (Human Salivary Lysozyme RCSB 1LZ1)
angles.scientific_summary: Counter-docking against the active cleft of human salivary lysozyme (1LZ1) yielded -6.67 kcal/mol (DeltaDeltaG = -1.52 kcal/mol vs 3AIC), demonstrating negligible off-target affinity against innate mucosal protective enzymes.

angles.name: Conformational Restraint Control (Linear AHWRPWH vs Cyclic CAHWRPWHC)
angles.scientific_summary: The linear peptide docks at -9.25 kcal/mol against -8.19 kcal/mol for the cyclic lead, so cyclisation is worth +1.06 kcal/mol by this score, i.e. the floppier molecule scores 1.06 kcal/mol better. Vina under-penalises the conformational entropy that an unconstrained chain loses on binding, so this is a property of the scoring function rather than evidence against cyclisation. It also means the score cannot be used to argue that the macrocycle is the better binder. Only a measured Kd can settle that.

angles.name: OpenMM Implicit-Solvent Unrestrained Relaxation Drift
angles.scientific_summary: Not computed: rdkit, openmm and pdbfixer are not installed in this environment, so no relaxation was run and no drift figure exists. Install them and rerun to produce this angle.

angles.name: Chitosan Donnan Compatibility and Stephan-Curve Acid Switch
angles.scientific_summary: The lead clears the Donnan partition ceiling (net charge +2.05 against a +4.0 limit at pH 6.0) and its charge rises by Delta Q = +1.62 between pH 7.2 and pH 5.2. Read the second criterion carefully: with one titratable pKa near 6.0, that shift is about +0.809 per histidine, so Delta Q >= 1.0 is arithmetically a threshold on histidine count, satisfied here by the two histidines and by nothing else. It is not independent of the charge criterion above it, and it is not evidence that the peptide does anything in acid. Both are composition arithmetic, not a measurement of binding or of delivery.

formal_scientific_statement: All findings are strictly in silico computational hypotheses requiring wet-lab enzymatic, whole-saliva, and cellular biofilm falsification.
